Stated intent is efficiency and parent empowerment (+1.0, +1.0), but actual operational outcome is the dismantling of centralized federal oversight and equity standards (-0.8, -0.9). Hypocrisy R_net = 8.50, driven by preemptive political framing masking structural erosion.
subject: McMahon plans to 'fire' herself out of a job, striving to show Congress that the Dept of Ed is not needed
posts: Linda McMahon aims to 'fire' herself by dismantling the Dept of Education, but is this administrative reshuffling or structural erasure? Evidence: Interagency transfers, state waivers, federal dissolution. #Education #USPol

McMahon claims transferring education functions to Labor and Treasury proves the cabinet department is redundant and will streamline funding directly to students and parents. Stated Judgement: (+1.0, +1.0) — Productive Manifestation 🌐

In practice, scattering federal education duties across executive agencies dismantles centralized civil rights enforcement and federal protections under a political pretext. Resulting Judgement: (-0.8, -0.9) — Exclusive Erasure

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception. Shifting administrative duties is weaponized as a pretext to dissolve federal oversight while masking the loss of equitable standards.

Integrity: Meaningful Distortion (Hypocrisy: 8.5, z: 3)
The Trump administration is actively dismantling the Department of Education, delegating programs to other executive bodies and encouraging states to seek federal waivers.

The Bright Side:
Streamlining administrative duplication could reduce bureaucratic waste, provided state-level equity standards remain robust.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The audit error confuses ADMINISTRATIVE EFFICIENCY (Q5) with STRUCTURAL ABOLITION (Q1), treating a bureaucratic reshuffle as systemic reform.

Social Physics Analysis:
This maneuver runs a classic Smart Selfish playbook: packaging a political ideology to dismantle federal oversight as an altruistic gift of efficiency to parents.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
Modal Dynamics: will be -> is not via Red Top (The Imperial Trap). A utopian promise of efficiency masks an extractive dismantling of public oversight.

The Unavoidable Truth: Decentralizing functions without safeguards dismantles federal civil rights enforcement in education.

The Unavoidable Lie: Shifting agency duties proves the Department of Education is entirely unnecessary.

Alethekanon:
Administrative restructuring is weaponized as a theatrical pretext to dismantle federal educational protections under the guise of local empowerment.

Awwthekanon:
Every student deserves a secure, well-funded path to learning, and political theater shouldn't gamble with their future stability.

Brothekanon:
They're literally speedrunning closing the education department by farming out homework to Treasury and Labor. Wild times.

Spirithekanon:
"A house divided against itself cannot fall by outside hands alone, but by the hollow pillars within." Tao Te Ching 32 PASS
True structures endure through integrity, not theatrical dismantlement.

aspects.reason: Administrative transfers mask the dismantling of federal oversight.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
McMahon plans to 'fire' herself out of a job, striving to show Congress that the Dept of Ed is not needed

Linda McMahon is shifting Department of Education functions to the Department of Labor and Treasury through interagency agreements as proof of concept.

Actual Article Body:
This material may not be published, broadcast, rewritten, or redistributed. ©2026 FOX News Network, LLC. All rights reserved. Quotes displayed in real-time or delayed by at least 15 minutes. Market data provided by Factset. Powered and implemented by FactSet Digital Solutions. Legal Statement. Mutual Fund and ETF data provided by LSEG.

Linda McMahon asks Congress to let her prove the Department of Education can be dismantled without disrupting federal student loans or K-12 funding.

U.S. Education Secretary Linda McMahon doubled down on closing the Department of Education (ED) as sought to demonstrate to Congress that the federal agency she leads is no longer necessary.

"Signing these interagency agreements means, in fact, that the Department of Education is contracting with these agencies to perform the functions that they've been given," McMahon told Fox News Digital. "The first big block of work was transferred over to the Department of Labor."

Throughout his 2024 presidential campaign, Donald Trump promised to eliminate the ED, later signing an executive order directing his administration to begin dismantling the agency.

MCMAHON EMBARKS ON FOUR-STATE TOUR TO PUT LOCAL LEADERS AND PARENTS 'BACK INTO THE DRIVER’S SEAT' OF EDUCATION

Education Secretary Linda McMahon outside the White House in Washington, D.C., on Tuesday, July 15, 2025. (Al Drago/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

As part of that effort, the Department of Labor (DOL) is taking on a major role in the day-to-day administration of adult education, family literacy, and career and technical education (CTE) programs under the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) and the Perkins Act. While Labor manages operational duties, the Department of Education retains statutory responsibilities and oversight while shifting services to states and grant recipients.

"It started first with CTE — Career and Technical Education — then K–12, and finally higher education as well," McMahon said.

McMahon explained that she wants to show lawmakers that federal support for students won't falter without a standalone cabinet department.

"I've asked Congress with this proof of concept in these interagency agreements: 'Let me prove to you that it works,'" she said. "Ultimately, Congress has to vote if we do close the Department of Education and if I, in fact, am able to fire myself. Hopefully, they will vote [for it], because I believe the outcome will be better for students — and that is the goal. That is certainly the president's goal."

TRUMP ADMIN URGES RETURNING EDUCATION TO STATES, CITING $3 TRILLION OF TAXES SPENT AND POOR PROFICIENCY SCORES

A Department of Education sign is displayed outside their federal student aid office on May 18, 2025, in Washington, D.C. (Kevin Carter/Getty Images)

The agency took another major step by partnering with the Department of the Treasury, which agreed to take over key operations related to federal student loans and collections on defaulted debt.

The student loan partnership with Treasury and the workforce initiative with DOL are part of a broader series of interagency agreements. According to Department of Education officials, the goal is to demonstrate a "proof of concept" to Congress that essential federal education functions and funding flows can be successfully reallocated across executive branch agencies without disruption.

"I call it my proof of concept to show Congress that it works, that the money still gets to schools and to students where they need it," McMahon told Fox News Digital.

"Some of the programs in the Department of Education were being duplicated in other agencies, or handled better elsewhere," McMahon added. "So let's be efficient. Let's make sure the money gets where it needs to go, let's measure that by student outcomes, and let's hold teachers and administrators accountable for what they're doing."

Andrew Gillen, a higher education policy research fellow at the Cato Institute, told Fox News Digital that shifting major core duties like student loans and formula grants marks a substantial change from previous interagency agreements, which historically focused on minor administrative support.

McMahon previously argued during the government shutdown that the ED acts primarily as a pass-through entity for federal money, contending that its day-to-day functions are nonessential.

"Congress appropriates the funds. The funds come through the Department of Education, and some of that funding still goes to other agencies to get to students and schools," McMahon told Fox News Digital. "Primarily, the money was passed through the Department of Education to then get to the states and local authorities for education."

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TARGETS HEAD START BUREAUCRACY IN MOVE ADVOCATES SAY PUTS PARENTS IN THE DRIVER'S SEAT

President Donald Trump holds up an executive order to start dismantling the Department of Education after signing it in the East Room of the White House in Washington, D.C., March 20, 2025.  (Mandel Ngan/AFP via Getty Images)

ED announced earlier this year that the agency moved out of the Lyndon B. Johnson Department of Education building, so the Department of Energy could move in by August. The move is what the officials call "a prudent step to save hundreds of millions of taxpayer dollars and further reduce the federal education bureaucracy."

The Trump administration is also seeking to reduce the department's footprint by returning more power to the states.

The ED launched a new process allowing states to seek greater flexibility in using federal education funds and reducing administrative burdens. Iowa became the first state to participate in the effort.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The Department of Education sent states a letter in July 2025 encouraging them to apply for the waiver, which would give state education officials more discretion over federal dollars and reduce compliance costs.

Joshua Q. Nelson is a reporter for Fox News Digital.

Joshua focuses on cultural trends, education, and public policy. He extensively covered reparations developments across the U.S., the Department of Education, and immigration issues.

Joining Fox News Digital in 2019, he previously graduated from Syracuse University's Maxwell School of Citizenship and Public Affairs and received the University of Pennsylvania's Wharton Public Policy Certificate.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
LAFD grilled over plans to spend $345M generated per year from proposed sales tax hike

LA Councilwoman Traci Park pressed the LAFD over plans to spend $345M annually from Measure FD as half of city fire stations exceed their lifespan.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

Los Angeles fire officials were grilled Friday over plans to spend $345 million a year from a proposed sales tax hike, as the department revealed more than half its stations are past their expected lifespan and crews can’t reach most city streets within the recommended four minutes.

With just 11 days before voters decide the fate of Measure FD, Councilwoman Traci Park and fellow councilmembers pressed Fire Chief Jaime Moore over how the department would spend the cash, fix fire stations and get more firefighters on the streets without wasting taxpayer dollars.

“If we are asking Angelenos to invest hundreds of millions of dollars into the fire department, City Hall owes them a concrete plan for how every dollar is going to make LA safer,” Park said.

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

Never miss a story

Park noted that the LAFD is operating with a budget approaching $1 billion, with its proposed 2026-27 spending plan totaling $939.5 million. The proposed half-cent sales tax hike would pump another $345 million annually into the department, potentially pushing its funding to nearly $1.3 billion.

But the department’s laundry list of problems is staggering.

Moore testified that 56 of LA’s 106 fire stations are between 50 and 85 years old, while six of the 22 maintenance hoists used to repair fire trucks at its Lincoln Heights facility are broken.

And buying new fire engines won’t deliver an overnight fix.

“It takes about three years for us to get a new fire engine,” Moore told the council.

California Post News: Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X, YouTube, WhatsApp, LinkedInCalifornia Post Sports Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, XCalifornia Post  Opinion California Post Newsletters: Sign up here!California Post App: Download here!Home delivery: Sign up here!Page Six Hollywood: Sign up here!

The department’s own analysis found its fire engines and ambulances can reach just 49.2% of city roads within four minutes, the recommended response-time benchmark.

LAFD has roughly the same number of firefighters as it did in the 1960s, despite emergency call volumes multiplying and the city’s population surging by 1.4 million people, according to firefighters who testified Friday.

Moore outlined plans to expand the next two firefighter recruit classes from a combined 120 to 180 recruits, but acknowledged the department doesn’t have enough civilian workers to process applicants or sufficient training infrastructure to rapidly expand hiring.

“We’re gonna have to hire more civilian staff,” Moore told council members, explaining that years of budget cuts had depleted the department’s support workforce.

Park zeroed in on whether City Hall could be trusted to keep the new tax money from disappearing into other spending priorities.

“Chief, are there mechanisms in place to prevent the Measure FD funds from being absorbed into the city’s general fund or being diverted for purposes other than fire department expansion?” she asked.

Moore said the measure includes protections preventing the revenue from being diverted to other city programs.

The United Firefighters of Los Angeles City union has already poured $4.5 million of its members’ money into campaigning for Measure FD, according to union secretary Ryan Quigley.

The proposal would raise LA’s sales tax from 10.25% to 10.75%, with no expiration date.

Park’s motion demands a detailed spending plan outlining which fire stations and equipment would be prioritized, how quickly additional firefighters could be hired and what improvements taxpayers could expect within 30, 60, 90 and 180 days.
